item.title: Appfest ft. Laron Huntley & The Gravely Brothers — Sat Oct 17, 2:00 PM — Wicked Weed Brewpub
item.description:
On Saturday, October 17 — Southern Appalachian Highland Conservancy will join the Appfest fun. We’re grateful to Wicked Weed Brewing for their ongoing support of our conservation work!
Join us for a great afternoon of Country, Americana and Southern Rock with Laron Huntley & the Gravely Brothers.
Shop local Appalachian makers with the Appalachian Makers Collective from 12–5 PM, then stick around for live music from 2–5 PM. Bring your people, support local artists, discover something new, and spend a Saturday celebrating the place we’re lucky to call home.
Laron Huntley & The Gravely Brothers, is a multi-generational band rooted in Asheville, NC with a sound steeped in classic country and southern rock. With deep local ties and a shared musical heritage, this group brings the authentic spirit of the mountains to every performance. Their show promises passion, talent, and timeless Americana vibes from heartfelt originals to crowd-pleasing covers and jam-worthy riffs.
Source: LiveMu

item.title: Asheville Symphony Presents - Masterworks 2: Nightfall — Sat Oct 17, 2:00 PM — First Baptist Church of Asheville
item.description:
Two performances, 2 p.m. and 8 p.m. Event Details and Tickets
SATURDAY, SEPTEMBER 26, 2026 2:00 P.M. AND 8:00 P.M. FIRST BAPTIST CHURCH OF ASHEVILLE Darko Butorac, conductor Joseph Conyers, double bass
There is a serene kind of beauty found only at twilight, when the landscape cedes to legend; this program lingers in these wild places at their most untamed and fragile. Anna Clyne’s stormy nocturne gathers “every shred of the luminous past” like “a naked woman running mad through the pure night.” Tan Dun’s spiritually cinematic Wolf Totem summons the mythical Mongolian wolf from the grasslands. Sibelius’s devastating Fifth conjures the inscrutable patterns of the aurora. Three works that find beauty in loss, solace in vast spaces, and mystery in the gathering dark. Clyne: This Midnight Hour Tan: Contrabass Concerto: Wolf Totem Sibelius: Symphony No. 5
Source: LiveMusicAsheville.com

item.title: Panthertown Great Wall Loop; the hike. — Mon Oct 19, 9:30 AM
item.description: Hendo Fun Friends Panthertown Valley, often referred to as the Yosemite of the East, visitors can enjoy deep gorges and broad valleys, mountain bogs and granitic rock domes, tranquil creeks and plunging waterfalls. Panthertown Valley is protected as part of the Panthertown-Bonas Defeat bear sanctuary. Rough terrain trails lead to 3 waterfalls and “the Great Wall’ pluton. Exceptional views. **Difficulty:** Immediate 300 ft descent into the valley. Short, steep descents to the base(s) of 3 waterfalls. Staircase-steep climb (400ft) to the top of the Great Wall Pluton followed by a steep descent. Natural surfaced trails with rocks & roots. 2 ea rock-hop stream xings (possibly wet). The last mile to the cars is a 300 ft ascent. Mountain Trolls are thieves; Zip your backpacks tight. We are the ***HFF Trail Trekkers***: We a’gonna get our step-counters a’workin’ !! item.title: Bent Creek--Rice Pinnacle--Stradley Mountain Loop 9.7 miles, 1300 ft ascent — Wed Oct 21, 8:00 AM
item.description: The Asheville Hiking Group **Trailhead: Rice Pinnacle, Bent Creek** **Description**: Good footing, mostly shaded, gradual ascent. Take the Deer Lake Lodge trail to Wolf Branch Trail to Ledford Trail (R) to Road 479 (R) to left on Rice Pinnacle Rd (491) and start of climb. At Ingles Field Gap take a sharp left on trail of the same name and ascend to Four corners--Stradley Mt. Take Little Hickory Top and descend to Ledford Gap and snack at picnic tables. Take Boyd Branch to Campground Connector, Bent Creek Gap Rd to Wesley Branch Trailhead. Deer Lake Lodge Trail back to Rice Pinnacle. Type: Loop. Max Elev: 3000'. Avg moving pace: 2.3 mph. Dogs on leash OK **Lunch is an option following the hike! Come join me for my last hike of the season before heading back to FL** \*\*COURTESY (Please read carefully!)\*\* Only sign up if you \\\*truly\\\* plan to come. item.title: Bull Creek & Swannanoa River, 6.6 mi, 400 ft elevation gain — Fri Oct 23, 9:00 AM
item.description:
The Asheville Hiking Group **[Sign-up opens 8:00 PM, Sunday October 18th]**
Our route for this hike loops around the Bull Creek Preserve before branching off onto the Dam Pasture Connector trail. This takes us to the Swannanoa River trail, then over to the lovely Warren Wilson campus. There, at around our halfway point, we'll take a snack and water break and return the same way.
The total distance is around 6.6 miles with a 425' elevation gain. We'll amble at a 2.5 mph clip. This is a relatively tame hike with a rating of about 3 on a 1-10 scale. Big shout-out to Todd for piecing this trail together and sharing it with me.
***Dog Policy:*** Dogs are extremely welcome but must be leashed.
***Guest Policy:*** If you'd like to bring a guest, they should join the Asheville Hiking Group and sign up for the hike on their own. Alternatively, contact me in advance and ask if it's okay to bring a "+1" after you've made it onto the "Going" list. Depending on timing and demand, I MAY be able

item.title: Blue Ridge Ecosystems – From Ice Age to the Present — Wed Nov 18, 1:00 PM
item.description: Blue Ridge Ecosystems – From Ice Age to the Present with Dan Lazar Wednesday, November 18 | 1 – 3pm BRN – Core | BREG – Elective Register Here! Blue Ridge ecosystems have changed dramatically since the end of the last ice age 18,000 years ago. For example, while glaciers still covered northern Ohio and Pennsylvania, the summits of the Great Craggy Mountains, the Black Mountains and the Smokies were treeless and clothed in alpine tundra vegetation, while Mastodons and Giant Ground Sloths roamed the valleys below. As the climate warmed, the plant and animal communities we see today slowly developed. Dan Lazar served for many years as the director of education at the Western North Carolina Nature Center, followed by several years as executive director of the Colburn Earth Science Museum. Dan has a degree in forest biology from the State University of New York College of Environmental Science and Forestry and has been an instructor in the Blue Ridge Naturalist program since 2005.

item.title: NOBODY'S DARLING STRING BAND — Sat Dec 5, 4:00 PM
item.description:
Nobody’s Darling String Band plays lively music in the old-time tradition at Jack of the Wood Pub every Saturday afternoon from 4-6pm.
Band Members include Dona Cavanagh, fiddle; Zena Rubin, banjo-uke; Maxine Herring, rhythm guitar; Hilary Dirlam, melody guitar; and Celia Millington-Wyckoff, bass.
The five women comprising Nobody’s Darling each have a long history of playing old-time music. Individually they have played in many other bands through the years, including The Carolina Oldtimers, The Pegtwisters, The Zuma House Band, Too Hot To Cook, The Luke Smathers Mountain Swing Band, Honey Holler, and The Carolina Chick Peas.
Stop in to enjoy the music and an afternoon libation or two, perhaps with an early supper or light bite . . . and don't forget your dancing shoes!

Do you want to take your remote working game to the next level? Do you find yourself saying wtf is Manifesting Self??
Well, you’re not alone. Remote working is glamorous, and also presents itself with challenges not seen in the traditional office environment.
Manifesting Self may sound a little out there. Trust me. It’s not. Whether we’ve been in the remote space for years, since the pandemic, or just recently, I’m certain it has changed each of us in ways we never thought possible. Let’s explore that together.
